title: Prefix and postfix increment

blocks.text: `i++` and `++i` both add one to `i`. They differ in the **value of the expression**: `i++` evaluates to the value *before* the increment, and `++i` to the value *after* it.
A `TicketDispenser` hands out numbered tickets, starting at `1`. Write its three methods, each a single `return` statement:

items: `take()` hands out the next number and moves on: the first call returns `1`, the second `2`.
`skip()` throws the next ticket away and returns the number `take()` will hand out now: on a new dispenser, `skip()` returns `2`, and `take()` then returns `2`.
`peek()` returns the number `take()` would hand out, and changes nothing.

cases.says: take() hands out 1, 2, 3 in order, and peek() changes nothing.
skip() returns the number after the skipped one: the value after the increment.

concepts: i++ evaluates to the old value and ++i to the new one.
